repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Direct, highly selective BTK inhibitor. Non-covalent binding to Cys481 with IC50 ~2 nM.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: BTK is an essential kinase for BCR and Fc receptor signaling. BTK inhibition reduces B cell activation, autoantibody production, and renal damage in lupus-prone mice. Fenebrutinib completed a Phase 2 trial in SLE (NCT02908100) showing reduction in CD19+ B cells and anti-dsDNA.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Irreversible covalent BTK inhibitor (Cys481). FDA-approved for B cell malignancies.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: Ibrutinib potently inhibits BTK with IC50 ~0.5 nM. Preclinical lupus models show reduced autoantibodies, proteinuria, and improved survival. Approved safety profile may facilitate repurposing, though cardiovascular and bleeding risks need monitoring.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Highly selective covalent BTK inhibitor. In development for multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: Selective BTK inhibition blocks B cell and myeloid cell activation relevant to SLE. Phase 2 trials in RA showed efficacy. B cell and myeloid targeting is theoretically attractive for lupus.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Selective allosteric TYK2 inhibitor binding to the pseudokinase (JH2) domain. FDA-approved for plaque psoriasis.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: TYK2 mediates type I IFN, IL-12, and IL-23 signaling â€” all central to SLE pathogenesis. Protective TYK2 loss-of-function variants reduce SLE risk. Deucravacitinib completed a Phase 2 trial in SLE (NCT03252587) showing numerical improvement in SRI-4 response. Direct target engagement is highly specific.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Allosteric TYK2 inhibitor. Blocks TYK2-mediated IRF5 activation downstream of TLR7/TLR9.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: IRF5 is activated by TYK2-dependent phosphorylation. TYK2 inhibition reduces IRF5-driven type I IFN production. This is an indirect but mechanistically strong approach since no direct IRF5 inhibitors exist. TYK2 sits directly upstream of IRF5 activation.
repurposing_candidates.evidence_level: Phase 2 in SLE; target pathway overlap

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: JAK1/2 inhibitor that blocks type I IFN and IL-6 signaling downstream of IRF5-mediated transcription.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: IRF5 drives IFN-Î± production; JAK1/2 inhibition blocks the signaling cascade downstream. Phase 3 SLE-BRAVE-I met primary endpoint (SRI-4). While not a direct IRF5 inhibitor, it blocks the consequences of IRF5 activation. Baricitinib is FDA-approved for RA and alopecia areata.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Blocks IFNAR1, the receptor for type I interferons. FDA-approved for moderate to severe SLE.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: IRF5 is the master transcription factor for IFN-Î±. Blocking IFNAR1 intercepts IRF5's downstream effects. Anifrolumab is already SLE-approved, providing a de-risked pathway. The IFN gene signature â€” largely driven by IRF5 â€” predicts anifrolumab response.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Binds the shared p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23, blocking STAT4-activating cytokines.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: STAT4 is the primary transcription factor activated by IL-12 and IL-23. Ustekinumab blocks the upstream cytokines that drive STAT4 phosphorylation. A Phase 2 trial in SLE (NCT02349091) met its primary endpoint (SRI-4 at week 24: 62% vs 33% placebo). Direct pathway inhibition with Phase 2 positive data.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Allosteric TYK2 inhibitor; TYK2 mediates IL-12/IL-23 â†’ STAT4 signaling.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: TYK2 is required for IL-12 and IL-23 receptor signaling. By inhibiting TYK2, deucravacitinib blocks STAT4 phosphorylation and downstream Th1/Th17 differentiation. Phase 2 in SLE showed encouraging signals.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Spleen tyrosine kinase (SYK) inhibitor. FDA-approved for chronic immune thrombocytopenia.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: SYK is a key downstream mediator of BCR signaling, the same pathway where BLK operates as an upstream Src-family kinase. SYK inhibition has shown efficacy in lupus-prone mice (reduced proteinuria, anti-dsDNA). Fostamatinib's B cell effects may partially compensate for BLK dysfunction.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: BTK inhibitor with potential cross-reactivity against BLK and other Tec family kinases.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: BLK and BTK are related kinases in BCR signaling. BTK inhibitors may partially compensate for defective BLK function by reducing overall BCR signal strength. Fenebrutinib has been studied in SLE.
repurposing_candidates.evidence_level: Phase 2 in SLE; kinase family overlap

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Proteasome inhibitor that blocks IÎºBÎ± degradation, suppressing NF-ÎºB activation. FDA-approved for multiple myeloma.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: TNFAIP3 (A20) normally inhibits NF-ÎºB by deubiquitinating key signaling intermediates. Loss-of-function TNFAIP3 variants in SLE result in unchecked NF-ÎºB activity. Bortezomib inhibits NF-ÎºB by preventing IÎºBÎ± degradation, partially compensating for A20 deficiency. Shown to deplete plasma cells in refractory SLE case series.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: JAK1/2 inhibitor with downstream effects on NF-ÎºB through cytokine signaling suppression.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: Multiple NF-ÎºB-driven cytokines (IL-6, TNF) signal through JAK-STAT. JAK inhibition reduces NF-ÎºB-mediated inflammation indirectly. Baricitinib's Phase 3 data in SLE provides clinical validation.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Blocks CD28-CD80/86 costimulation, the second signal required for T cell activation after MHC-TCR engagement.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: HLA-DRB1 presents autoantigens to CD4+ T cells â€” the initiating event in lupus autoimmunity. Abatacept blocks the costimulatory signal that follows MHC-TCR engagement. Phase 2b in SLE showed benefit in arthritis; Phase 3 in lupus nephritis narrowly missed primary endpoint but showed improvement in serological markers. Strong mechanistic rationale.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Polyclonal IgG that saturates FcRn, enhances immune complex clearance, and modulates FcÎ³R expression.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: ITGAM mutations impair phagocytosis via complement receptor 3 (CR3). IVIG enhances FcÎ³R-mediated phagocytosis and immune complex clearance, potentially compensating for defective CR3 function. IVIG is used clinically in severe refractory SLE though evidence is from case series.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Blocks the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), reducing IgG recycling and lowering pathogenic autoantibody levels.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: FCGR2A variants impair IgG immune complex clearance, leading to accumulation of pathogenic immune complexes. FcRn blockade reduces total IgG (including autoantibodies) by 60-80%, decreasing the substrate for immune complex formation. Phase 2 trials in SLE and lupus nephritis ongoing.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: FcRn inhibitor reducing pathogenic IgG levels, decreasing ADCC substrate and immune complexes.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: FCGR3A (CD16a) mediates ADCC and immune complex clearance. Impaired FCGR3A function leads to immune complex accumulation. FcRn blockade reduces the IgG autoantibody pool, decreasing the burden on an already-impaired clearance system.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Engineered Fc fragment that competes for FcRn binding, accelerating IgG degradation. FDA-approved for myasthenia gravis.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: Same FcRn blockade rationale as nipocalimab. Reduces total IgG and autoantibodies, decreasing immune complex burden on FCGR3A-mediated clearance. Approved safety profile facilitates repurposing.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: SYK inhibitor that blocks BCR signaling downstream of BANK1 scaffold protein.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: BANK1 is a scaffold protein that modulates BCR-induced calcium mobilization. SYK is the immediate downstream kinase from BCR engagement. While not a direct BANK1 inhibitor (which doesn't exist), SYK inhibition reduces the BCR signal that BANK1 amplifies.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Blocks CD28 costimulation, raising the threshold for T cell activation â€” compensating for PTPN22-mediated dysregulation.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: PTPN22 (LYP) is a phosphatase that raises the TCR signaling threshold. The R620W gain-of-function variant further suppresses TCR signaling, paradoxically allowing autoreactive T cells to escape negative selection. Abatacept raises the activation threshold for all T cells, which may help normalize the altered selection. Indirect but mechanistically interesting.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Directly binds and neutralizes OX40 ligand (TNFSF4), blocking T cell costimulation through OX40-OX40L axis.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: TNFSF4 (OX40L) is upregulated in SLE and directly drives Tfh responses and autoantibody production. Oxelumab is a direct anti-OX40L antibody. Phase 2 trials in SLE were initiated. This is the most direct approach to targeting TNFSF4-driven pathology.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Blocks CD40L-CD40 costimulation, an alternative T-B cell interaction axis to OX40-OX40L.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: T cell costimulation in SLE occurs through multiple redundant pathways. Blocking CD40L-CD40 â€” another key T-B interaction â€” may partially compensate for OX40L overexpression. Dapirolizumab pegol showed positive Phase 2b results in SLE (2024). Pathway-level intervention.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: FcRn antagonist reducing pathogenic IgG autoantibody levels.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: Reducing total IgG autoantibodies decreases immune complex burden, compensating for impaired FCGR2A-mediated clearance. Efgartigimod is FDA-approved for gMG with a well-characterized safety profile.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: FcRn inhibitor reducing IgG immune complex levels.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: ITGAM mutations impair CR3-mediated phagocytosis. Reducing immune complex load via FcRn blockade decreases the burden on defective clearance mechanisms. Complementary approach to IVIG.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Blocks IFNAR1, the shared receptor for all type I interferons. FDA-approved for moderate to severe SLE.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: TYK2 is required for IFNAR1 signaling â€” it is the kinase that transduces the type I IFN signal from the receptor to STAT1/STAT2. Blocking IFNAR1 with anifrolumab achieves functional TYK2 pathway inhibition at the receptor level. Anifrolumab is already FDA-approved for SLE with demonstrated efficacy in reducing disease activity and corticosteroid use. The IFN gene signature, which is TYK2-dependent, predicts anifrolumab response.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: JAK1/2 inhibitor with partial activity against TYK2 at higher concentrations. FDA-approved for RA and alopecia areata.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: TYK2 and JAK1 form heterodimers to mediate type I IFN signaling. Baricitinib inhibits JAK1 â€” the obligate partner of TYK2 in IFNAR signaling â€” thereby indirectly blocking the pathway TYK2 participates in. Phase 3 data in SLE (SLE-BRAVE-I) met its primary endpoint. While less selective than deucravacitinib, baricitinib has more extensive clinical data in SLE.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: JAK1/2 inhibitor that blocks cytokine signaling downstream of T cell activation following MHC-TCR engagement.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: HLA-DRB1 presents autoantigens to CD4+ T cells, which then produce cytokines that signal through JAK-STAT pathways. Baricitinib intercepts this cascade by blocking the cytokine signaling that follows T cell activation, effectively targeting the consequences of HLA-DRB1-mediated autoantigen presentation. Combined baricitinib plus abatacept could provide dual blockade of both the costimulatory and cytokine signals downstream of MHC-TCR engagement.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Inhibits calcineurin, blocking NFAT dephosphorylation and preventing IL-2 transcription in T cells activated through MHC-TCR engagement.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: HLA-DRB1 presents autoantigens that activate autoreactive CD4+ T cells. Cyclosporine blocks the calcineurin-NFAT pathway that is the primary signaling cascade triggered by TCR engagement following MHC-peptide recognition. This directly interrupts the functional consequence of HLA-DRB1-mediated autoantigen presentation. Cyclosporine has decades of clinical use in transplantation and autoimmune disease, with known efficacy in lupus nephritis.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Highly selective, irreversible BTK inhibitor with improved safety profile vs ibrutinib. FDA-approved for CLL and MCL.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: BANK1 amplifies BCR signaling by scaffolding downstream effectors including BTK. While BANK1 itself is not directly druggable, inhibiting BTK â€” the kinase immediately downstream in the BCR signalosome â€” reduces the signal that BANK1 amplifies. Acalabrutinib's improved selectivity reduces off-target kinase inhibition compared to ibrutinib, potentially offering a better safety profile for chronic autoimmune use.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Type II anti-CD20 antibody with enhanced direct cell death and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity vs rituximab.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: BANK1 dysfunction promotes B cell hyperresponsiveness and autoantibody production. B cell depletion with obinutuzumab â€” which showed positive Phase 3 results in lupus nephritis (REGENCY trial, 2024) â€” eliminates the cellular substrate for BANK1-mediated pathology. This is an upstream approach that removes the B cells where BANK1 operates rather than targeting the pathway downstream. The REGENCY trial provides SLE-specific clinical validation.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Pan-JAK inhibitor (JAK1 > JAK3 > JAK2) that broadly suppresses cytokine signaling downstream of TCR engagement. FDA-approved for RA, PsA, and UC.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: PTPN22 gain-of-function variants paradoxically promote autoimmunity by altering T cell selection thresholds. Tofacitinib raises the effective threshold for T cell activation by blocking the cytokine signals (IL-2, IL-4, IL-21) that amplify T cell responses after TCR engagement. This may help normalize the altered selection landscape created by PTPN22 dysfunction. Tofacitinib has an extensive safety database from its approved autoimmune indications.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Inhibits calcineurin-NFAT pathway, blocking IL-2 production and raising the threshold for productive T cell activation.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: PTPN22 gain-of-function reduces TCR signal strength, paradoxically allowing autoreactive T cells to evade negative selection. Cyclosporine raises the threshold for TCR-mediated T cell activation by blocking calcineurin-NFAT signaling â€” the primary calcium-dependent pathway downstream of TCR engagement. This directly counteracts the consequence of PTPN22 dysfunction at the T cell activation level. Approved for decades with extensive clinical experience including off-label use in lupus nephritis.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Pan-JAK inhibitor that blocks JAK-mediated STAT4 phosphorylation downstream of IL-12 and IL-23 receptors.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: STAT4 is phosphorylated by JAK2 and TYK2 following IL-12 and IL-23 receptor activation. Tofacitinib inhibits JAK family kinases including JAK2, reducing STAT4 activation and Th1/Th17 differentiation. While less selective than TYK2-specific approaches, tofacitinib's broader JAK inhibition may provide more comprehensive suppression of STAT4-activating pathways. Extensive safety data from approved indications supports repurposing feasibility.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Highly selective irreversible BTK inhibitor. Blocks BCR signaling downstream of Src-family kinases including BLK.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: BLK is a Src-family kinase that initiates BCR signaling by phosphorylating ITAM motifs on CD79a/CD79b. BTK is the kinase immediately downstream that propagates the signal. Inhibiting BTK with acalabrutinib intercepts the signaling cascade that BLK initiates, partially compensating for BLK dysfunction. Acalabrutinib's improved kinase selectivity vs ibrutinib may reduce off-target effects in chronic autoimmune use.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Activates the Nrf2 antioxidant pathway and downregulates NF-ÎºB through multiple mechanisms including inhibition of nuclear translocation. FDA-approved for multiple sclerosis.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: TNFAIP3 (A20) normally suppresses NF-ÎºB through ubiquitin editing. Loss-of-function TNFAIP3 variants in SLE result in chronic NF-ÎºB activation. Dimethyl fumarate inhibits NF-ÎºB through a complementary mechanism â€” Nrf2 activation and glutathione depletion reduce NF-ÎºB nuclear translocation â€” effectively providing an orthogonal path to NF-ÎºB suppression that doesn't depend on functional A20. Approved safety profile in MS with over a decade of post-marketing experience.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Selective C5a receptor antagonist that blocks C5a-mediated neutrophil activation, migration, and adhesion. FDA-approved for ANCA-associated vasculitis.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: ITGAM encodes CD11b, a subunit of complement receptor 3 (CR3) that mediates phagocytosis and immune complex clearance. When CR3-mediated clearance is impaired, deposited immune complexes activate the complement cascade, generating C5a â€” a potent anaphylatoxin that recruits neutrophils and drives tissue inflammation. Avacopan blocks C5aR on neutrophils, intercepting the inflammatory amplification loop that follows defective CR3-mediated clearance. Approved for complement-driven autoimmune vasculitis with a targeted safety profile.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Blocks the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), reducing IgG recycling and accelerating pathogenic IgG degradation. FDA-approved for myasthenia gravis.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: FCGR2A variants (H131R) reduce IgG2 binding affinity and impair immune complex clearance. Rozanolixizumab reduces total IgG by ~70%, decreasing the substrate for immune complex formation and the burden on FCGR2A-mediated clearance. This FcRn antagonist offers an alternative mechanism to nipocalimab and efgartigimod with an approved safety profile.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Long-acting monoclonal antibody that binds C5 and blocks cleavage into C5a and C5b-9 (MAC), preventing terminal complement activation. FDA-approved for PNH and atypical HUS.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: FCGR3A variants impair IgG-mediated immune complex clearance, leading to tissue deposition of immune complexes that activate complement. C5 cleavage generates C5a (driving neutrophil recruitment and inflammation) and C5b-9/MAC (causing direct tissue damage). Ravulizumab blocks terminal complement activation at C5, intercepting the downstream tissue damage that follows impaired FCGR3A-mediated clearance â€” without affecting the upstream clearance pathways that other approaches target. Approved with strong safety data in complement-mediated diseases.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Blocks CD40-CD40L interaction, preventing T cell-dependent B cell activation and germinal center formation.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: TNFSF4 (OX40L) promotes Tfh responses driving autoantibody production; CD40-CD40L is a parallel T-B costimulation axis. Blocking CD40 provides an alternative approach to controlling T cell help for autoreactive B cells when OX40-OX40L is overactive. Iscalimab has shown promising results in SjÃ¶gren's syndrome and renal transplantation, with Phase 2 data in autoimmune disease.

repurposing_candidates.mechanism: Humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds BDCA2 (CLEC4C) on plasmacytoid dendritic cells, inhibiting TLR7/TLR9-induced IFN-Î± and proinflammatory cytokine production at its cellular source.
repurposing_candidates.rationale: BDCA2 is a C-type lectin receptor selectively expressed on plasmacytoid dendritic cells â€” the primary producers of IFN-Î± in SLE. BDCA2 engagement triggers ITAM-BCR-like inhibitory signaling that suppresses TLR7/TLR9-mediated IFN-Î± production. Litifilimab directly targets this pathway, reducing the type I interferon gene signature that is present in ~60-80% of SLE patients. The Phase 2 LILAC trial (NCT02847598) demonstrated significant reduction in active joint count and skin disease (CLASI). Now in Phase 3 TOPAZ program. This is a direct gene-targeted therapy â€” the strongest possible repurposing candidate for BDCA2.
repurposing_candidates.evidence_level: Phase 2 completed in SLE (LILAC); Phase 3 ongoing (TOPAZ)
